true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Duplicate downsize method definitions break the previous API

Ruby does not support method overloading. The second downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) definition replaces the preceding four-argument downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) definition. The old width/height API becomes dead code, and any existing caller using four positional size arguments will now pass the fourth argument as opts or raise an argument error.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-side upload limit is hardcoded to 10 MB

The client validation replaces Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] with a fixed 10 MB limit. This ignores the configured max_image_size_kb and max_attachment_size_kb values, so users can attempt uploads that are not allowed (especially attachments), and configurations with limits above or below 10 MB are no longer respected in the UI.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Animated-image handling depends on temporary file extension

OptimizedImage.optimize selects the animated code path only when the input path ends in .gif. The controller downsizes temporary upload paths that may not preserve the original extension, so animated GIFs can be processed with convert file[0] and flattened to a single frame. The supplied '80%' dimension is also an ImageMagick-style geometry and may not be valid for gifsicle.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
413 error message uses a hardcoded 10 MB limit

The 413 handler now reports a fixed 10 MB maximum size instead of using the relevant site setting. If the actual limit differs, users receive an inaccurate error message.

In-place downsizing uses the same input and output path

OptimizedImage.downsize is called with tempfile.path as both source and destination. ImageMagick or gifsicle may truncate or corrupt the file while reading and writing the same path, and the boolean return value is ignored. A failed conversion can therefore leave a corrupted or zero-byte upload that is then passed to Upload.create_for.

Nil tempfile is not handled before calling tempfile.size

If FileHelper.download fails, tempfile is nil because of rescue nil. The code then calls Upload.create_for with tempfile.size, which raises NoMethodError instead of returning a graceful upload error.

No tests cover the new automatic downsizing behavior

The PR changes upload limits and mutates uploaded files, but adds no tests for the downsizing loop, failed conversions, files that remain oversized, SVG/GIF edge cases, or the changed OptimizedImage.downsize API. These are high-risk paths that can corrupt uploads or bypass configured limits.

Remote download limit is hardcoded to 10 MB

FileHelper.download now uses 10.megabytes instead of a site-setting-based limit for URL uploads. The later automatic downsizing only applies to recognized images, so non-image URL uploads, or images when the size setting is disabled, are no longer constrained by the configured limit at this stage.

SVG files are sent through raster downsizing

The new block downsizes every file accepted by FileHelper.is_image?, but does not exclude SVG. Elsewhere, OptimizedImage.create_for explicitly copies SVGs instead of resizing them. Running ImageMagick convert on an SVG can rasterize or corrupt the vector image while keeping the original filename, producing a damaged upload.

Upload proceeds even if the image is still too large after five attempts

The loop makes at most five 80% resize attempts and then falls through without checking whether the file is now within SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. If the file is still oversized, or if re-encoding fails to reduce size, the code continues to Upload.create_for, risking an oversized stored image or an expensive delayed failure.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation mutates host without guarding against nil

EmbeddableHost's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! unconditionally. If host is nil, for example from a malformed admin API request, this raises NoMethodError before validations can run. The callback should guard against blank/nil host, and the model should have an explicit presence validation.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Update and destroy assume the embeddable host record exists

Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy use EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first without checking for nil. If an unknown id is supplied, update calls save_host(nil) and destroy calls host.destroy, causing a NoMethodError and a 500 response instead of a 404.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Existing embeddable hosts are migrated without normalization

The migration copies old embeddable_hosts lines verbatim into embeddable_hosts.host. The new model only strips scheme and path in an ActiveRecord before_validation callback, which migrations bypass. Existing values like http://example.com, https://example.com/path, or blank lines will be stored as-is or as empty rows. Since EmbeddableHost.record_for_host later compares only the URI host against lower(host), these migrated rows may never match, silently breaking embedding after upgrade.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration interpolates old site setting values into raw SQL

The INSERT statement embeds the old embeddable_hosts setting line directly into SQL: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). A stored value containing a single quote or SQL fragment can break the migration or execute unintended SQL. These values should be inserted through parameterized SQL or at least connection.quote.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration can crash when expected site setting rows do not exist

The migration indexes directly into the first row of raw SQL results: execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i. On fresh installs, or on sites where embed_category was never changed, the site_settings row will not exist, so [0] is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError. The same unsafe pattern is used at line 15 for uncategorized_category_id. This can block the migration completely.

false_negatives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

false_positives.candidate:
Category ID is accepted without validating that the category exists

save_host assigns category_id directly from request parameters and only replaces it when blank. A nonexistent numeric category id, or category_id=0, can be persisted. TopicEmbed.import later uses EmbeddableHost#category_id when creating topics, so invalid category references can cause data integrity problems or failed topic creation.

Host format regex rejects valid hostnames

The validation regex restricts the top-level domain to [a-z]{2,5}. This rejects valid modern domains with longer TLDs, such as .travel or .agency, and also prevents using localhost in development. The host validation is more restrictive than necessary for the feature.

Hosts saved with a port will never match incoming referers

The host validation regex allows an optional port, so example.com:8080 can be saved. However record_for_host parses the incoming URL with URI and compares only uri.host, which excludes the port. As a result, a configured host with a port will never match http://example.com:8080/, making port-specific host entries unusable.

New admin endpoints have no functional controller coverage

The specs for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController only assert controller inheritance. There are no tests for create/update/destroy behavior, invalid ids, malformed parameters, host normalization, category handling, or the data migration. Given the number of edge cases in this feature, this is a significant test gap.

No uniqueness constraint or validation on host

EmbeddableHost does not validate uniqueness of host, and the migration does not create a unique index. Duplicate host rows can therefore be created. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host uses where(...).first without an order, so if duplicates exist with different categories, the category used for imported topics is arbitrary.

PUT /admin/customize/embedding does not update anything

Admin::EmbeddingController#update ignores all request parameters and simply renders the current embedding object. The client defines a saveChanges action that issues this update, but the endpoint cannot persist any embedding-level changes. If no attributes are intended to be editable here, the route/action should be removed or the endpoint should be implemented.

Plural embedded ID hydration can create undefined records or throw

_hydrateEmbedded assumes any key ending in _ids is an array and calls obj[k].map. If the payload contains null or undefined for that key, this throws. If some IDs cannot be found via _lookupSubType, the resulting association array contains undefined entries, and the original *_ids key is deleted anyway. UI code iterating that association may then fail.

Saved host category is set from local selection instead of server response

After saving, the component sets host.category using Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')). If the selected category was blank and the server normalized it to the uncategorized category, or if the local categoryId is undefined, the UI may display the wrong category or no category. It should use the category_id returned in the saved host payload.

resources :embeddable_hosts exposes routes with no controller actions

resources :embeddable_hosts generates index, show, new, edit, create, update, and destroy routes, but Admin::EmbeddableHostsController only implements create, update, and destroy. Requests to the extra routes will result in missing action errors. The route should be restricted to only the implemented actions.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists

TopicsController#unsubscribe calls TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) and immediately reads tu.notification_level. If the current user has no topic_users row for that topic (for example they never visited the topic, the row was removed, or the URL is visited directly), find_by returns nil and the action raises NoMethodError instead of handling the unsubscribe. Use find_or_initialize_by, or TopicUser.change, so a missing row is created or handled safely.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Direct TopicUser save bypasses notification-change side effects

TopicsController#unsubscribe updates the TopicUser record directly and calls save!, bypassing TopicUser.change. TopicUser.change is the normal path for notification-level changes and sets notifications_changed_at/notifications_reason_id and publishes the notification_level_change MessageBus event. With the direct save, open clients will not be notified of the new notification level, and the reason/audit metadata for the change is lost. It also does not handle the missing-row case the way TopicUser.change does.

No specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint

The PR adds a state-changing TopicsController#unsubscribe endpoint but includes no controller/request specs. Important cases are untested: missing TopicUser row, slug mismatch redirects, JSON vs HTML behavior, permission handling, and the fact that the action mutates notification state. A spec would catch the nil TopicUser crash and the missing MessageBus/metadata behavior.

Shared unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for all callers

The shared `unsubscribe_link` translation now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Email::MessageBuilder renders this translation for any email built with `add_unsubscribe_link`, but only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` was updated to supply `unsubscribe_url`. Any other current/future caller or plugin that enables the unsubscribe link without providing `unsubscribe_url` will fail email rendering/sending with a missing interpolation argument. Make the per-topic line conditional, provide a default, or update all callers.

State-changing unsubscribe is performed by an unauthenticated GET

The new /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe endpoint changes the user's topic notification level in response to a GET request, skips the XHR check, and has no token or confirmation. Because Rails CSRF protection does not apply to GET requests, a third-party page can cause a logged-in user to mute or downgrade notifications for arbitrary topic IDs by loading an image or link. Email prefetching or link previews can also trigger the change unintentionally. Use a POST/PUT action, a signed per-user unsubscribe token, or at least require an explicit confirmation step.

track_visit! uses the topic id as the user id when passed an id

TopicUser.track_visit! computes user_id as `user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic`. When the second argument is a user id integer, as in TopicsController#track_visit_to_topic (`TopicUser.track_visit! topic_id, user_id`), the method assigns the topic id to user_id. This creates or updates topic_users rows for the wrong user, corrupting visit tracking and potentially notification-related state. The else branch should return `user`, not `topic`.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
should_block? writes statistics during validation and can double-count

should_block? loads a BlockedEmail row, increments match_count in Ruby, and saves it while being called from an ActiveModel validator. In UsersController#create, user.valid? is called and then user.save runs validations again, so one signup attempt can increment the same blocked-email row twice. The read-modify-write is also non-atomic, so concurrent requests can lose increments. Move counting out of the predicate or use an atomic counter update once per request.

true_positives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Domain whitelist regex is not anchored and can be bypassed

email_in_restriction_setting? builds a case-insensitive regex of the form @(domains) without anchoring the domain to the end of the address and escapes only dots. With a whitelist of example.com, an address such as user@example.com.evil.com matches the regex and is accepted, defeating the whitelist. The same pattern can also overmatch blacklisted domains. Parse the domain list explicitly, escape regex metacharacters, and anchor each allowed or blocked domain.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked email lookup and uniqueness are not normalized

BlockedEmail.should_block? queries the exact email string, and the model does not downcase or strip the address before validation or storage. If an admin blocks bad@example.com, a signup using Bad@Example.com, or the same address with surrounding whitespace, will not match and will bypass the block. The uniqueness validation and database index are also case-sensitive, allowing duplicate blocked rows that differ only by case. Normalize emails before saving and querying.

false_positives.candidate:
Blocked email specs do not cover normalization or controller integration

The specs only exercise exact-case matches, and the validator spec stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? rather than testing the real flow. There is no test that a User save is rejected when a blocked email is supplied with different casing or whitespace, nor a request/controller test that the signup endpoint actually blocks creation and returns the expected error. Add integration-level coverage for these paths.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage origin check uses substring matching

The listener accepts messages when `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) !== -1`. This is not an exact origin comparison; an origin that is a prefix or substring of `discourseUrl` can pass. Compare `e.origin` against the parsed origin of `discourseUrl` exactly.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Imported URL is interpolated into raw HTML footer without escaping `TopicEmbed.import` appends `"#{url}"` to imported content. The URL is only loosely checked and is not HTML-escaped. Since imported posts use the `raw_html` cook method and are rendered with `raw`, a malicious URL containing quotes, tags, or script can produce stored XSS.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Invalid ERB `end if` will prevent the template from rendering

The first conditional is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which compiles to invalid Ruby (`end if` is not legal). Rendering the `best` embed view will raise a syntax error. It should be a plain `<% end %>`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed items without content crash the poller

`i.content.scrub` assumes every feed item has a content field. RSS/ATOM items may have only description/summary or nil content, causing `NoMethodError`. With `retry: false`, the scheduled job stops. Handle nil content and fall back to other item fields.

true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-controlled Referer is interpolated into JavaScript without JavaScript escaping

The embed layout outputs `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. The Referer header is controlled by the embedding page and is not escaped for JavaScript. A crafted referer can break the script context or potentially inject JavaScript into the Discourse origin, and it also controls the postMessage target origin. Use `escape_javascript`/`to_json` and validate the target origin explicitly.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

false_positives.candidate:
Adding `force: true` to the top_topics migration can drop data

Changing `create_table :top_topics` to use `force: true` makes the migration drop and recreate the table if rerun. This can silently delete existing `top_topics` data. Migrations should not destructively recreate tables that may already contain production data.

Check-then-create embed can raise unique-index errors under concurrency

`import` checks for an existing `TopicEmbed` and then creates one, while the database has a unique index on `embed_url`. Concurrent first imports of the same URL can both pass the check; one will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. Rescue the unique violation and reload/use the existing record.

Embed content SHA is updated even if the revision fails

After `PostRevisor#revise!`, `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` runs unconditionally. If the post cannot be revised or saved, the stored SHA no longer matches the post content, causing future content changes to be skipped. Check the revision result before updating the SHA.

Post side effects are enqueued before the outer embed transaction commits

Inside `Topic.transaction`, `PostCreator#create` runs and enqueues jobs/publishes messages after its own inner transaction but before the surrounding `TopicEmbed` transaction commits. If `TopicEmbed.create!` later fails and the outer transaction rolls back, asynchronous work remains queued for records that were not persisted.

Redis throttle key is set and expired non-atomically

`$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` is not atomic. If the process crashes between the two calls, the key can remain without TTL and permanently throttle retrieval for that embed URL. Use an atomic SET with NX and expiration.

Script throws if `discourse-comments` element is absent

`document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` may return null on pages that include `embed.js` but do not have the expected container. The subsequent `comments.appendChild(iframe)` throws and prevents the embed from loading. Guard against the missing element.

URL scheme validation uses line-start anchor instead of string-start anchor

`return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` uses `^`, which in Ruby matches the beginning of any line. A multiline string containing a non-http scheme followed by a newline and an http URL can pass this check. Use `\A` (and preferably validate the whole URL) to enforce the scheme.

`absolutize_urls` can raise on borderline URLs

`URI(url)` is called without rescuing `URI::InvalidURIError`. The preceding URL check only requires an http(s) prefix, so strings with spaces or other invalid characters can reach this method and crash import/retrieval jobs. Validate or rescue invalid URLs and skip them.

`force: true` will drop an existing topic_embeds table

The migration creates `topic_embeds` with `force: true`, which drops the table first. If the table already exists from a prior installation or branch, existing embed mappings are destroyed. Avoid `force: true` in migrations that may run against existing data.

`import_remote` opens the URL before validating scheme or safely restricting it

`TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` before `TopicEmbed.import` applies its http/https check, and `TopicRetriever` only compares the URI host to `embeddable_host`. A URL with a matching host but non-HTTP scheme can reach `open`, allowing unintended fetches or local file access if an open-uri handler supports it. Validate scheme and URL format before opening.

`import` assumes `contents` is a non-nil mutable string

`TopicEmbed.import` immediately mutates its `contents` argument with `contents << ...`. If a caller passes nil (possible from feed/readability extraction) or a frozen string, the import raises instead of failing cleanly. Validate or normalize the content before appending.

`raw_html` cook method bypasses sanitization and is rendered raw

The new `cook` path returns `raw` unchanged when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Imported external HTML is untrusted, and the embed view renders `post.cooked` with `raw`. Without sanitization this enables stored XSS from feeds or retrieved embed pages.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items mixin has incomplete/invalid legacy flexbox prefixes

The `align-items` mixin omits `-moz-box-align` even though `flexbox()`/`inline-flex()` emit `-moz-box`/`-moz-inline-box`, so old Mozilla box implementations will not receive the alignment. It also emits the non-existent `-ms-align-items` property and does not map modern values such as `flex-start`/`flex-end` to the legacy `start`/`end` values. Add `-moz-box-align`, remove `-ms-align-items`, and map values if legacy support is intended.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order mixin does not convert values for legacy ordinal groups

Legacy 2009 flexbox ordinal groups (`-webkit-box-ordinal-group`, `-moz-box-ordinal-group`) are 1-based, while the standard `order` property is 0-based and can be negative. Passing `$val` unchanged can produce incorrect or invalid ordering in browsers that use the legacy prefixes. Convert the value for those prefixes (for example, add 1 for non-negative orders) or avoid exposing the raw standard value.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.

false_positives.candidate:
Button in .small-action will no longer be right-aligned

Adding `@include flexbox()` to `.small-action` makes its direct children flex items. The existing `button` rule still uses `float: right` (line 309), but float is ignored on flex items, so the button will not be pushed to the right edge as it was in the float-based layout. Use `margin-left: auto`, `order`, or a spacer element to position the button.

Header flex container may overflow because flex-wrap is not set

`.d-header .contents` is converted to a flex container without setting `flex-wrap`. Flexbox defaults to `nowrap`, so header children such as the title, extra topic info, and panel will stay on one line and can overflow horizontally on narrow viewports, unlike the previous float-based layout that could drop/wrap. Add `flex-wrap: wrap` or appropriate responsive constraints if wrapping is required.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Inclusion guard is missing the question mark

include_website_name will not be used by ActiveModel::Serializer, which looks for include_website_name?. As written, the serializer includes website_name unconditionally, even when website is blank, yielding a null field. Rename the method to include_website_name? and base it on the presence of the value that should be exposed.

false_positives.candidate:
Domain comparison treats unrelated hosts as same

The same-domain check drops only the first label of each hostname and compares the rest. This treats unrelated hosts such as forum.co.uk and example.co.uk, or a.github.io and b.github.io, as the same domain, so the serializer will append the website path when it should display only the host. The logic is also asymmetrical for example.com vs www.example.com. Use a proper registrable-domain comparison or a simpler exact/subdomain rule.

Untrusted attribute test does not cover website_name

The spec's untrusted_attributes list was not updated to include :website_name, so it does not verify that the new derived field is hidden for TL0 users viewed anonymously. Since website is untrusted, the test should also assert that website_name is omitted.

website_name can become stale after profile edits

The template now binds to model.website_name, but that value is generated on the server and is not recomputed when model.website changes. User#save only updates bio_excerpt from the response, so after editing a profile website the displayed website name can remain stale until a reload. The previous controller computed property observed model.website and avoided this.

website_name leaks website data for restricted TL0 users

UserSerializer adds :website_name to the public attributes but does not add it to untrusted_attributes, unlike :website. When an anonymous or low-trust viewer sees a TL0 user, restrict_user_fields? hides website, but website_name is still serialized. Because website_name is derived from the hidden website, it exposes the user's website host/path. Add :website_name to untrusted_attributes and update the spec.

true_positives.golden_comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Embedded-post author link color appears inverted, reducing contrast

The rule for .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a previously used scale-color($primary, 30%). It was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 70%), scale-color($secondary, 30%)), which makes the light-theme color much lighter and the dark-theme color much darker. Comparable author/name links use 30% in light schemes and 70% of $secondary in dark schemes, so this looks reversed and will make the link faint in both themes.

true_positives.golden_comment: In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.
true_positives.matched_candidate:

true_positives.golden_comment: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
findMembers allows an offset equal to the total member count

findMembers clamps offset to Math.min(user_count, offset), but the last valid offset is generally user_count - limit. Allowing offset == user_count requests an empty page. This can happen after deleting the last member on the last page or via the pagination next logic, leaving the UI showing no members.

true_positives.golden_comment: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
remove_member automatic-group spec uses the wrong HTTP verb

The automatic-group case for remove_member uses xhr :put, but the route is defined as DELETE and the successful remove_member spec uses DELETE. This test does not exercise the real HTTP verb/route and could miss routing regressions.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
totalPages is off by one for exact multiples of limit

totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is exactly divisible by limit, such as 50 users with limit 50, it returns 2 pages instead of 1. This allows the UI to navigate to an empty extra page.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

false_positives.candidate:
Admin groups API contract changed without compatibility

The previous admin groups API accepted a nested group payload, allowed usernames during create/update, and supported incremental membership changes via PATCH. The new controller expects flat parameters and separate membership endpoints. Existing clients or plugins using the old admin group API may fail or silently lose membership changes.

Group member item view template name appears wrong

The view sets templateName to 'admin/templates/group_member'. Discourse/Ember template names are normally registered without the 'templates' segment, e.g. 'admin/group_member'. If the resolver follows that convention, this view will not find its template and each member item will render blank even if the each helper is fixed.

Group members endpoint accepts unbounded and negative pagination values

The members action uses params[:limit].to_i and params[:offset].to_i without validating bounds. A client can request an extremely large limit, causing a large database query and serialization, or negative limit/offset values, which can trigger database errors. This is an availability risk on an endpoint that may be accessible to non-admin users.

Member list uses an invalid non-block each helper

The template uses {{each member in members itemView="group-member"}} without the block form {{#each ...}} and without a closing {{/each}}. In Ember/Handlebars this will not render the collection (or may fail to compile), so the admin group page will not display members even though the controller/model load them.

add_members silently ignores invalid or whitespace-padded usernames

add_members splits the usernames string and only adds users found by User.find_by_username. It does not strip whitespace and does not report unknown usernames. If some or all usernames are invalid, the action still returns success, so the admin UI indicates members were added when they were not.

create ignores alias_level sent by the client

The client sends alias_level when creating a group, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible. Any alias level selected while creating a new group is discarded, and the group is created with the default alias level.

update resets visible to false on partial updates

update unconditionally sets group.visible based on whether params[:visible] equals 'true'. Any API client that updates only some fields, such as name, without also sending visible will unintentionally hide the group. This makes partial updates unsafe and changes the previous API behavior.

true_positives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsynchronized initialization/read of @loaded_locales

`ensure_loaded!` initializes and checks `@loaded_locales` outside `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `load_locale` mutates the same array inside the mutex. Under multithreaded servers this can race, causing duplicate loads or lost/cleared loaded-locale state. Initialize the array in a thread-safe way and perform the check under the same mutex.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
Fallback list ignores hash storage and assignments

`FallbackLocaleList` subclasses Hash but overrides `[]` to always recompute the chain and never consult stored entries. Normal fallback customization such as `I18n.fallbacks[:zh_TW] = [:zh_CN, :en]` will silently have no effect. If fallbacks are intended to be extensible, the class should merge stored/custom entries or expose an explicit extension point.

Fallback locales are only loaded for controller requests

The accelerator loads translation data lazily, and `translate` only calls `load_locale(config.locale)`. The new fallback locales are loaded only by `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!`, which is invoked solely from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any server-side translation outside that controller path (background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, `I18n.with_locale` blocks, or errors before the filter) will not have the fallback locale YAML loaded, so missing keys may not actually fall back to `SiteSetting.default_locale` or `:en`.

Translation cache key omits fallback order/default locale

After this change, the result of a cached translation can depend on `SiteSetting.default_locale` (and the hardcoded `:en` fallback), but the cache key is only key + current locale + backend object id. If the default locale changes and `I18n.reload!` is not called, cached missing-key translations will continue to return the old fallback language. Include the fallback chain/default locale in the cache key or ensure invalidation on fallback changes.

Unconditional call to custom `ensure_loaded!` can raise

`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` assumes the fallbacks object is the custom `FallbackLocaleList`. If another initializer, plugin, or test replaces `I18n.fallbacks` with a standard fallback object, every request will raise NoMethodError. Consider calling it only when `I18n.fallbacks.respond_to?(:ensure_loaded!)`.

true_positives.golden_comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Call to undefined method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()

UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments. The superclass UsernamePasswordForm only defines isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) in this PR, and no no-argument method exists in this class or its parents. This is a compile-time error. The intended call is likely isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), or a no-arg helper needs to be added.

true_positives.golden_comment: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Conditional passkey setup is skipped when no user is known

isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) returns false unless user != null. Both authenticate (line 115) and the error challenge override (line 137) use this method to decide whether to call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context). On the initial login screen and after errors such as unknown username, context.getUser() is null, so the WebAuthn conditional UI challenge/attributes are not set. This regresses passkey login from the first login form and contradicts tests that expect the webauth form on the initial page.

true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator uses unsupported negative QuerySet slicing

When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, the code sets start_offset to the negative offset and executes queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices, so this raises an AssertionError rather than performing efficient reverse pagination. Because cursor offsets are parsed from client input, a crafted cursor can trigger a 500 on endpoints using this paginator. Negative offsets should be rejected or handled without negative QuerySet slices.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate AuditLogEntry.datetime

The endpoint selects OptimizedCursorPaginator while ordering by -datetime. Unlike DateTimePaginator, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on the field value and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value instead of converting it to a datetime. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so the first non-empty optimized page raises TypeError when build_cursor computes a key, and any non-zero cursor would also filter a datetime column with a numeric value. This makes the optimized pagination path fail with 500 or invalid queries. Use DateTimePaginator or make OptimizedCursorPaginator handle datetime conversion.

false_negatives.golden_comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
Importing non-existent OptimizedCursorPaginator

false_positives.candidate:
BasePaginator change allows invalid negative offsets for prev cursors

The new start_offset calculation uses cursor.offset unchanged when cursor.is_prev is true. Cursor.from_string accepts negative integers, so a cursor like 0:-1:1 causes queryset[-1:stop], which Django QuerySets do not support, leading to a 500 on any BasePaginator-derived endpoint. For non-prev cursors, negative offsets are silently coerced to 0, which can mask malformed input and return the wrong page. Cursor offsets should be validated as non-negative.

Extra-row drop condition compares against an impossible length

In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, after slicing from start_offset, results can contain at most limit + extra rows, but the code checks len(results) == offset + limit + extra. When cursor.offset is greater than zero, this condition cannot be true, so the extra row fetched for backward pagination may not be removed. This can return one too many rows or produce incorrect prev-cursor state. The check should compare against the number of rows actually requested, e.g. limit + extra or stop - start_offset.

No tests for the new pagination path

The PR introduces a query-parameter-controlled paginator switch and a new paginator with cursor, datetime, and negative-offset behavior, but no tests. At minimum, tests are needed for the optimized audit-log endpoint covering empty and non-empty pages, next and prev cursors, malformed or negative offsets, and permission fallback when optimized_pagination is absent or the user lacks access. Without tests, these failure modes are easy to regress.

Typo order_b prevents changing queryset ordering

In BasePaginator.build_queryset, when converting an existing descending order to ascending, the code assigns to queryset.query.order_b instead of queryset.query.order_by. The intended ordering change is silently lost, so previous-page pagination can query in the wrong order and return incorrect results. This affects BasePaginator and its subclasses used by the new optimized path.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative offset slicing in OptimizedCursorPaginator will crash

When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the queryset with a negative start offset and possibly a negative stop offset. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing, so this raises AssertionError. Since cursor offsets come from client-provided cursor strings and the audit-log endpoint enables advanced features, an authorized user can trigger a 500.

true_positives.golden_comment: In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
BasePaginator now passes negative prev offsets to QuerySet slicing

The new start_offset logic uses cursor.offset directly when cursor.is_prev is true. If a client supplies a negative offset in a previous-page cursor, the queryset is sliced with a negative offset. Django QuerySets do not support negative offsets, so this raises AssertionError. This affects all BasePaginator subclasses, including DateTimePaginator.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Optimized paginator is incompatible with datetime ordering

The endpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime'. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on the field value and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value, while AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime. Any non-empty optimized page will raise TypeError, and the cursor value would also be compared to a timestamp column as an integer.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

false_positives.candidate:
Changing span-buf:s:* keys from sets to sorted sets is not migration-safe

The PR changes span buffer keys from Redis sets (SADD/SCARD/SSCAN) to sorted sets (ZADD/ZCARD/ZSCAN) while keeping the same key names. Existing in-flight keys written by the old code can remain for up to redis_ttl, default 3600 seconds. New ZADD/ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZSCAN operations on those set-typed keys will return WRONGTYPE errors, causing span buffering and flushing failures during rollout.

Consumer assumes end_timestamp_precise is present and valid

process_batch indexes val['end_timestamp_precise'] and passes it directly to Redis ZADD as a score. If a message lacks the field, has null, or has a non-numeric value, the consumer raises KeyError/TypeError and processing stops. Since this field is newly required by the buffer, invalid or older messages need validation or a safe fallback.

No tests cover eviction, large segments, or sorted-set migration

The updated tests only add end_timestamp_precise to small segments. They do not create more than 1000 spans, do not verify which spans are evicted by score, do not test duplicate-member ZUNIONSTORE behavior, and do not cover interaction with old set-typed keys. Given the new data-dropping behavior, this is a significant test gap.

Optimized audit-log pagination path has no tests

The new optimized_pagination branch and OptimizedCursorPaginator are not covered by tests. Given the datetime incompatibility and negative-offset crash paths, this endpoint/paginator combination needs explicit tests before merging.

Redirect-chain limit reduced to 1000 may split deep traces

The redirect resolution loop was lowered from 10000 to 1000. If a redirect chain is longer than 1000, the script stops early and maps the span to an intermediate set, which can prevent related spans from being merged into the same segment. This trades correctness for bounded runtime and should be documented or metered.

Silent eviction can drop spans, including root spans, and ignores configured limits

The Lua script uses ZPOPMIN to remove the lowest-scored members whenever a segment has more than 1000 spans. This silently discards spans, can evict the root/segment span while leaving the has_root_span flag set, and bypasses the Python max_segment_spans configuration. There is no metric or log, so incomplete segments can be produced without observability.

Typo prevents reversing queryset ordering for previous pages

In BasePaginator.build_queryset, when converting an existing '-key' ordering to ascending for a previous page, the code assigns to queryset.query.order_b instead of queryset.query.order_by. The queryset ordering is therefore not changed, so previous-page pagination can query with the wrong ORDER BY and return incorrect results. This affects paginators built on BasePaginator, including the new OptimizedCursorPaginator.

ZUNIONSTORE default SUM can corrupt span scores

The Lua script uses ZUNIONSTORE without specifying AGGREGATE. If the same span payload/member exists in both source sorted sets, Redis sums the end_timestamp_precise scores. The corrupted score changes eviction order and can prevent the span from being evicted when expected. An explicit AGGREGATE MAX or MIN should be used.

max_segment_spans parameter is now ignored

SpansBuffer still accepts and stores max_segment_spans, but the new Lua script hardcodes the cap at 1000 and the Python flush path no longer enforces max_segment_spans. Callers configuring this parameter will get a different silent limit and a behavior change from skipping oversized segments to evicting spans.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling decision uses the original dataset/request instead of the query actually executed

`_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset`, and may later execute a modified query such as a dashboard-split query (`... AND !event.type:transaction` or `... AND event.type:transaction`). However the upsampling eligibility check is computed from the outer `dataset` and the original HTTP request only: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)`. It does not consider the actual `scoped_dataset` or the final `query` being executed. This can cause the `count()` rewrite to be applied to a transaction-like query, or skipped for an error-only split query, leading to incorrect counts or query failures. The eligibility check should be based on the actual dataset and query passed to the query executor.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

false_positives.candidate:
Accidental submodule/gitlink added to repository root

The PR adds a file named `sentry-repo` containing a Git subproject commit pointer. This looks like an accidental embedded repository/submodule rather than an intentional source change. There is no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry or documented reason for it, and it can break clones, CI checkouts, and tooling that does not expect an embedded repository at the repo root. It should be removed from the PR.

Cache key construction sorts and hashes all project IDs on every call

The cache key is built with `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))` before checking whether the dataset/query is even eligible for upsampling. For organizations with many projects, this adds sorting and hashing overhead to every events-stats request, including datasets where upsampling is never applied. A cheaper early-out for non-applicable datasets, or a more efficient stable key, would avoid undermining the stated performance optimization.

Eligibility cache can serve stale upsampling decisions and invalidation is not wired

`is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches project allowlist eligibility for 60 seconds keyed by organization and project set. If the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option changes during that window, especially when a project is removed from the allowlist, queries can continue to use upsampled counts incorrectly. The provided `invalidate_upsampling_cache` helper is not called from anywhere, and it only invalidates one exact project-set key rather than all affected keys. This creates a data-integrity window after configuration changes. Include a config/version token in the cache key or wire up broader invalidation.

Endpoint tests do not exercise the explicit `errors` dataset path

The upsampling helper unconditionally applies for the `errors` dataset, but the added endpoint tests only use the default/discover path and one explicit `dataset=discover` case. There is no test with `dataset=errors`, so the branch where the rewrite is always enabled for the errors dataset is not covered. This is important because the new SnQL function was added in the discover dataset configuration and the errors-dataset behavior may differ.

Substring check for `event.type:error` can misclassify discover queries

`_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the raw query string contains the substring `event.type:error`. This is unsafe for Sentry search syntax: it matches negated queries such as `!event.type:error`, compound queries such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, and text inside quoted values. For the discover dataset this enables `upsampled_count()` for mixed or non-error event queries, where `sample_weight` may be missing, zero, or inapplicable, producing silently incorrect counts. The check needs to parse/understand the query rather than using a raw substring match.

`upsampled_count` assumes valid integral `sample_weight` values

The new `upsampled_count` aggregate is implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. This has two data-correctness risks: (1) if any event in an allowlisted project has a NULL/missing/zero `sample_weight`, the contribution can be dropped or become zero even though the event exists; (2) if `sample_weight` can be fractional, `toInt64` truncates the summed result and biases counts downward. Project-level allowlisting does not by itself guarantee every event has a valid integral weight. Consider using an explicit fallback such as `coalesce(sample_weight, 1)` and avoiding lossy integer casting unless weights are guaranteed integral.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes dict order matches input order

nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids) returns a dict, and the code zips error_ids with events.values(). If get_multi omits missing keys or returns them in a different order than the input node_ids, the zip will associate error data with the wrong event IDs. The resulting ErrorEvent objects would have mismatched id/title/message/timestamp. A safer approach would be to iterate over zip(error_ids, node_ids) and look up each node_id in the returned dict explicitly.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
TableWidgetVisualization rendered with hardcoded empty data behind feature flag

When the 'use-table-widget-visualization' feature flag is enabled, the component renders TableWidgetVisualization with columns=[] and tableData containing empty data/meta. This means any table widget will appear completely empty when the flag is on, regardless of actual query results. The actual result.data, result.meta, fields, and other computed props are ignored. This appears to be placeholder/incomplete code that should not be merged in its current state.

true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Mutual exclusivity validation uses truthiness, fails for age=0 or timestamp=0

validate_timestamp checks `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and validate_age checks `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. Since IntegerField allows 0 (timestamp has min_value=0, age has no min_value), a report with both age=0 and timestamp=123 would pass validation because `0` is falsy. The check should use `"age" in self.initial_data` or `self.initial_data.get("age") is not None` to correctly detect field presence.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

false_positives.candidate:
get_recommended_event() called per issue inside PR comment generation loop

get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() for each of the top issues (up to 5) during PR comment body construction. get_recommended_event typically hits nodestore/snuba and can be expensive. Since this runs inside get_comment_body which is called in a webhook/task context, the cumulative latency could be significant. Consider fetching environments in batch or caching the result.

get_request_data mutates the input error_events list in-place

error_events.sort(key=lambda x: x["timestamp"]) modifies the caller's list. While currently the list is request-scoped and used only once, this hidden side effect makes the function fragile: any future caller that reuses the list after calling get_request_data will observe an unexpectedly reordered sequence. Consider sorting a copy: sorted(error_events, key=...).

isLoading reports true during background refetches, not just initial load

The hook sets isLoading: isFetching, which is true on every refetch (e.g., window focus, query key change), not only on the initial load. Consumers that show a full loading spinner based on isLoading will flash unnecessarily. Consider using isPending or isInitialLoading from useQuery, or exposing both isLoading and isFetching separately.

request.user.id may crash when authenticated via org auth token

The analytics record call uses user_id=request.user.id unconditionally. When the request is authenticated with an org auth token (checked later via is_org_auth_token_auth), request.user may be None or an anonymous user without an id attribute. Since the analytics attribute is defined as required=False, the fix should be something like user_id=getattr(request.user, 'id', None) or a conditional check before accessing .id.

true_positives.golden_comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup codes are compared case-sensitively and without trimming

The server only removes dashes before doing `indexOf`. Generated codes are lowercase hex, while the UI placeholder uses uppercase. Normalize by trimming, removing separators, and lowercasing before comparison. The same issue exists in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Two parallel successful logins can read the same array before either update completes; one update can overwrite the other, restoring an already-used code, or the same code can be accepted by both requests. One-time backup codes are therefore not guaranteed to be single-use. Use a transaction/row lock or an atomic consumption mechanism.

If the user closes the dialog with Escape/overlay/close affordance, `onOpenChange` closes the modal without calling `onEnable`, even though 2FA has already been enabled server-side. Backup code input is assumed to be a string

A malformed POST with a number/object/array for `backupCode` will throw a TypeError and return a 500 instead of a validation error. Backup-code sign-in can bypass password/first-factor verification

In the CredentialsProvider authorize function, the password is verified only when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The backup-code path at line 131 is taken whenever `credentials.backupCode` is present. A caller can therefore POST credentials containing a valid `backupCode` and an arbitrary non-empty `totpCode`; the password check is skipped and the backup code alone authenticates the user. For password accounts this removes the password factor, and for non-CAL identity-provider accounts it also bypasses the OAuth/SAML first factor. Consequence: account takeover if a backup code is known or leaked.

Modal state reset does not clear react-hook-form/TOTP value

The PR adds UI for backup codes and server-side consumption, but the tests only verify that the codes are displayed/copied/downloaded. Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the show/hide password button prevents keyboard users from focusing and activating it. This makes the password field less accessible; the control should remain focusable or provide an equivalent keyboard-accessible alternative.

Submitting an empty backup-code form can fail silently

The login form has `noValidate`, so the BackupCode input's required/minLength attributes are not enforced. If a user is on the lost-access screen and submits an empty backup code, the server falls back to the TOTP branch and returns `second-factor-required`; the client merely keeps the two-factor screen and displays no error, leaving the user stuck. Show an error or validate the backup code client-side before submitting.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

The computed keys in minimumTokenResponseSchema (e.g. [z.string().toString()]) do not create a catch-all/index signature in Zod; they only add fixed, unintended properties. As a result, when app credential sharing is enabled, normal OAuth fields such as refresh_token, expires_in, expiry_date, and provider-specific fields are stripped from the parsed token. This causes loss of token data and broken refresh flows. Use z.record/catchall or an explicit schema.

false_positives.candidate:
Find-then-create/update credential is not atomic

The endpoint performs findFirst followed by create/update without a transaction or unique-constraint upsert. Concurrent webhook calls for the same user/app can both miss an existing credential and create duplicate credentials, or overwrite each other in an undefined order. This can cause stale or ambiguous OAuth credentials. Use atomic updateMany/create or a transaction with proper uniqueness.

No automated tests for credential sync webhook

This adds a security-sensitive webhook that can create/replace OAuth credentials and changes token refresh flows across many apps, but no automated tests are included for authentication, encryption/decryption, invalid payloads, duplicate handling, or sync-enabled refresh behavior. Without tests these regressions are easy to reintroduce.

Outbound credential sync request has no authentication or HTTPS enforcement

The outbound request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug and does not include a shared secret, signature, or client authentication. It also does not require HTTPS. If the endpoint is reachable outside a trusted internal network, it can be abused to obtain user tokens, and token responses may be exposed in transit. Add authentication/signing and enforce HTTPS.

Salesforce client refreshes token unconditionally

getClient always calls the Salesforce OAuth token endpoint before creating a connection, even if the stored access token has not expired. This creates unnecessary refresh requests and can cause rate limiting or latency. Check the token expiry and refresh only when needed.

Updating synced credential does not clear invalid flag

The webhook update path only updates key. If the existing credential has invalid: true from a previous failed refresh, the newly synced valid key remains marked invalid and may be skipped by adapters. The update should also set invalid: false when accepting new synced credentials.

Webhook handler accepts all HTTP methods

The handler does not check req.method. A GET or other non-POST request will still execute the webhook logic and likely throw during body parsing, returning a 500 instead of a 405. Restrict the route to POST.

Zoom refresh uses wrong app slug

The sync helper is called with appSlug 'zoomvideo', but the Zoom app credential is stored/identified by the slug 'zoom' (for example, the OAuth callback creates appId 'zoom'). The external sync endpoint will receive an unrecognized app slug and may return the wrong token or fail. Use 'zoom'.

prisma is used but not imported

The added credential update calls prisma.credential.update, but the file does not import prisma from @calcom/prisma. This will fail type checking or throw a ReferenceError at runtime when the Salesforce calendar service attempts to refresh credentials.

Any exception is treated as an SMS scheduling failure, including failures after Twilio scheduling

The catch block increments retryCount for every error, including errors thrown by the database update after `twilio.scheduleSMS` has already succeeded.
