false_positives.candidate:
Async legacy writes use the request context and will be canceled when the request finishes

DualWriterMode3.Create starts a goroutine to write to legacy storage and derives its context from the incoming request context via context.WithTimeoutCause. When the API request handler returns, the request context is canceled, which cancels the async legacy write. The same pattern exists in Delete (line 110), Update (line 135), and DeleteCollection (line 163). Since mode 3 is explicitly asynchronous, the legacy operation should use a detached context, for example context.WithoutCancel plus a timeout, or a background context with copied logger/values; otherwise legacy writes may be aborted before completion.

Asynchronous legacy writes can execute out of order

Each mutating operation spawns an independent goroutine for the legacy write with no sequencing, completion tracking, retry, or backpressure. A client can issue update or delete immediately after create; the legacy update/delete may execute before the legacy create, fail, or a delayed legacy create may recreate an object after a delete. This makes the legacy store inconsistent and can resurrect deleted objects despite mode 3 being intended as a safe dual-write fallback. A per-resource serialized queue or other ordering guarantee is needed.

Legacy update re-evaluates the update instead of writing the unified storage result

In Update, after Storage.Update succeeds, the goroutine calls Legacy.Update with the original rest.UpdatedObjectInfo. Legacy.Update will retrieve the legacy object's current state and invoke objInfo.UpdatedObject against that state. For patch-style updates, or if the legacy store is behind, this can produce a different result than the unified update or fail. The previous implementation wrapped the object returned by the unified update so legacy received the exact final object. Passing the original objInfo risks inconsistent legacy data and unsafe use of request-scoped update info after the request completes.

Legacy object is not deleted when unified delete returns NotFound

Mode3.Delete returns immediately if Storage.Delete returns any error, including NotFound, so it never attempts Legacy.Delete. If an object exists only in legacy storage because of earlier async failure, mode transition, or legacy-only residue, deleting it through the API will leave the legacy object behind. The prior behavior still attempted legacy deletion when unified deletion returned NotFound.

Async legacy create uses the original object without a deep copy

The Create goroutine passes the same runtime.Object to Legacy.Create that was passed to Storage.Create and may be the same object returned to the caller. Kubernetes storage strategies can mutate objects during create, and the response may be serialized while the legacy goroutine is running. This can cause data races or inconsistent legacy writes. Use runtime.DeepCopyObject, preferably copying the final object that should be written to legacy, before starting the goroutine.

Destroy can run while async legacy writes are still in flight

Destroy closes both Storage and Legacy immediately, but Mode 3 methods start detached goroutines that can continue to call Legacy for up to 10 seconds. If shutdown or Destroy happens while those goroutines are running, they may use closed storage, fail, or race. Track outstanding goroutines with a WaitGroup or worker pool and wait for them in Destroy.

Mode 3 integration test checks legacy APIs immediately after asynchronous writes

The added mode 3 integration subtest runs doPlaylistTests, which creates, updates, and deletes through the k8s API and immediately queries legacy endpoints. Because mode 3 writes to legacy asynchronously, those immediate legacy reads can race and make the test flaky. The test needs polling or eventual-consistency checks for mode 3, or it should not assert synchronous legacy visibility.

Mode3 tests race with asynchronous legacy writes and do not verify them

The Mode 3 unit tests invoke mutating methods that start goroutines but do not wait for or assert the legacy calls. In TestMode3_Delete at line 230 and TestMode3_DeleteCollection at line 284, no legacy mock expectation is configured, yet the async goroutine will call Legacy.Delete or Legacy.DeleteCollection; this can panic or produce nondeterministic results. Even where expectations exist, tests do not verify async behavior. Add synchronization and AssertExpectations.

Legacy async failures are only counted, not logged

Async legacy errors are only passed to metrics. For example, if Legacy.Create fails in the goroutine, there is no log entry; the old synchronous code logged such failures. Silent legacy-write failures make divergence and operational problems hard to detect. Log the error with object kind/name and cause.

`TopicEmbed.import` immediately mutates its `contents` argument with `contents << ...`. If a caller passes nil (possible from feed/readability extraction) or a frozen string, the import raises instead of failing cleanly. Validate or normalize the content before appending.

`raw_html` cook method bypasses sanitization and is rendered raw

The new `cook` path returns `raw` unchanged when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Imported external HTML is untrusted, and the embed view renders `post.cooked` with `raw`. Without sanitization this enables stored XSS from feeds or retrieved embed pages.

`import_remote` opens the URL before validating scheme or safely restricting it

`TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` before `TopicEmbed.import` applies its http/https check, and `TopicRetriever` only compares the URI host to `embeddable_host`. A URL with a matching host but non-HTTP scheme can reach `open`, allowing unintended fetches or local file access if an open-uri handler supports it. Validate scheme and URL format before opening.

Post side effects are enqueued before the outer embed transaction commits

Inside `Topic.transaction`, `PostCreator#create` runs and enqueues jobs/publishes messages after its own inner transaction but before the surrounding `TopicEmbed` transaction commits. If `TopicEmbed.create!` later fails and the outer transaction rolls back, asynchronous work remains queued for records that were not persisted.

Check-then-create embed can raise unique-index errors under concurrency

`import` checks for an existing `TopicEmbed` and then creates one, while the database has a unique index on `embed_url`. Concurrent first imports of the same URL can both pass the check; one will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. Rescue the unique violation and reload/use the existing record.

Redis throttle key is set and expired non-atomically

`$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` is not atomic. If the process crashes between the two calls, the key can remain without TTL and permanently throttle retrieval for that embed URL. Use an atomic SET with NX and expiration.

Embed content SHA is updated even if the revision fails

After `PostRevisor#revise!`, `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` runs unconditionally. If the post cannot be revised or saved, the stored SHA no longer matches the post content, causing future content changes to be skipped. Check the revision result before updating the SHA.

`absolutize_urls` can raise on borderline URLs

`URI(url)` is called without rescuing `URI::InvalidURIError`. The preceding URL check only requires an http(s) prefix, so strings with spaces or other invalid characters can reach this method and crash import/retrieval jobs. Validate or rescue invalid URLs and skip them.

`force: true` will drop an existing topic_embeds table

The migration creates `topic_embeds` with `force: true`, which drops the table first. If the table already exists from a prior installation or branch, existing embed mappings are destroyed. Avoid `force: true` in migrations that may run against existing data.

Adding `force: true` to the top_topics migration can drop data

Changing `create_table :top_topics` to use `force: true` makes the migration drop and recreate the table if rerun. This can silently delete existing `top_topics` data. Migrations should not destructively recreate tables that may already contain production data.

Script throws if `discourse-comments` element is absent

`document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` may return null on pages that include `embed.js` but do not have the expected container. The subsequent `comments.appendChild(iframe)` throws and prevents the embed from loading. Guard against the missing element.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

true_positives.reasoning: The candidate's main point is about the file extension, but it also says '80%' geometry may not be valid for gifsicle on the animated path. That is the same issue as the golden comment.

false_positives.candidate:
413 error message uses a hardcoded 10 MB limit

The 413 handler now reports a fixed 10 MB maximum size instead of using the relevant site setting. If the actual limit differs, users receive an inaccurate error message.

FileHelper.download now uses 10.megabytes instead of a site-setting-based limit for URL uploads. The later automatic downsizing only applies to recognized images, so non-image URL uploads, or images when the size setting is disabled, are no longer constrained by the configured limit at this stage.

The PR changes upload limits and mutates uploaded files, but adds no tests for the downsizing loop, failed conversions, files that remain oversized, SVG/GIF edge cases, or the changed OptimizedImage.downsize API. These are high-risk paths that can corrupt uploads or bypass configured limits.

If the current user has no topic_users row for that topic (for example they never visited the topic, the row was removed, or the URL is visited directly), find_by returns nil and the action raises NoMethodError instead of handling the unsubscribe. true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: find_by returns nil when no TopicUser record exists, so calling a method on tu raises NoMethodError, a nil pointer crash.

false_positives.candidate:
State-changing unsubscribe is performed by an unauthenticated GET

The new /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe endpoint changes the user's topic notification level in response to a GET request, skips the XHR check, and has no token or confirmation. Because Rails CSRF protection does not apply to GET requests, a third-party page can cause a logged-in user to mute or downgrade notifications for arbitrary topic IDs by loading an image or link. Email prefetching or link previews can also trigger the change unintentionally. Use a POST/PUT action, a signed per-user unsubscribe token, or at least require an explicit confirmation step.

Direct TopicUser save bypasses notification-change side effects

TopicsController#unsubscribe updates the TopicUser record directly and calls save!, bypassing TopicUser.change. TopicUser.change is the normal path for notification-level changes and sets notifications_changed_at/notifications_reason_id and publishes the notification_level_change MessageBus event. With the direct save, open clients will not be notified of the new notification level, and the reason/audit metadata for the change is lost. It also does not handle the missing-row case the way TopicUser.change does.

TopicUser.track_visit! computes user_id as `user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic`. When the second argument is a user id integer, as in TopicsController#track_visit_to_topic (`TopicUser.track_visit! topic_id, user_id`), the method assigns the topic id to user_id. This creates or updates topic_users rows for the wrong user, corrupting visit tracking and potentially notification-related state. The else branch should return `user`, not `topic`.

Shared unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for all callers

The shared `unsubscribe_link` translation now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Email::MessageBuilder renders this translation for any email built with `add_unsubscribe_link`, but only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` was updated to supply `unsubscribe_url`. Any other current/future caller or plugin that enables the unsubscribe link without providing `unsubscribe_url` will fail email rendering/sending with a missing interpolation argument. Make the per-topic line conditional, provide a default, or update all callers.

No specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint

The PR adds a state-changing TopicsController#unsubscribe endpoint but includes no controller/request specs. Important cases are untested: missing TopicUser row, slug mismatch redirects, JSON vs HTML behavior, permission handling, and the fact that the action mutates notification state. A spec would catch the nil TopicUser crash and the missing MessageBus/metadata behavior.

false_positives.candidate:

getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups CalendarCache rows only by credentialId and does not filter on expiresAt, while getCachedAvailability only treats rows with expiresAt >= now as valid. As a result, the connected-calendars API can report a cacheUpdatedAt timestamp for a credential whose cache entries are all expired, causing the UI to show stale cache status and offer delete actions based on invalid data. Add an expiresAt: { gte: new Date() } condition or otherwise exclude expired rows.

Handler bypasses calendar-cache factory/mock

connectedCalendarsHandler directly instantiates CalendarCacheRepository instead of using the cache initialization path used elsewhere, which can select a mock or disabled behavior for calendar cache. This can query the real CalendarCache table and expose cache status even in environments or feature configurations where calendar caching is supposed to be disabled or mocked, and it makes tests that rely on the mock ineffective. Use the same cache factory/abstraction used by the rest of the calendar-cache code.

Delete-cache mutation does not refresh connected calendars data

The deleteCache mutation only calls the optional onSuccess prop after success; it does not invalidate trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, unlike the disconnect mutation. If the parent does not provide an onChanged handler that invalidates or refetches, the UI will continue to display the old cacheUpdatedAt value after cache deletion. Invalidate the connected-calendars query in onSuccess or onSettled.

Empty actions container rendered when dropdown has no items

ConnectedCalendarList always wraps CredentialActionsDropdown in a div with fixed width and right alignment. When the dropdown returns null, for example for delegation credentials with no cache status, the empty container still occupies layout space in the card or alert actions area. Render the wrapper conditionally or move the container inside CredentialActionsDropdown so it can return nothing without leaving an empty spacer.

credentialId schema accepts any number

The deleteCache input uses z.number() for credentialId, which allows negative, zero, and non-integer values. Credential IDs are positive integers, so use z.number().int().positive() to reject invalid input early.

dev:cron depends on npx tsx without declaring tsx

The dev:cron script now invokes npx tsx cron-tester.ts, but tsx is not declared as a dependency or devDependency. npx may download it on demand or prompt interactively, making the script network-dependent and less reproducible. In checkIfIsAvailable, end is computed from slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime, so event length is ignored and slots extending past working hours can pass. Additionally, workingHours.find returns true if any same-day working-hours range does not contain the slot, so multiple ranges can reject a valid slot, and if no range matches the day the code falls through and may return true.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Day.js objects are compared with ===

The code checks dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...). Day.js instances are objects, so === compares identity and is always false. The intended start-equals-end unavailable-date case is never detected, which can incorrectly mark slots as available.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same bug: Day.js objects compared with ===, which checks reference identity, so the comparison is always false. The candidate also explains the consequence of that bug.

false_positives.candidate:
Date override path skips busy-time checks

In checkIfIsAvailable, when a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot is not rejected by the override bounds, the function returns true before executing the busy.every check. Existing bookings and calendar busy times inside date overrides are therefore ignored, which can allow double bookings.

Multiple date overrides on the same day are handled incorrectly

checkIfIsAvailable uses dateOverrides.find and returns true from the callback as soon as the slot is outside a same-day override. If a user has multiple date overrides on the same day, a slot inside a later override but outside the first one will be rejected. The logic should check whether the slot is contained in at least one override instead of rejecting on the first non-matching override.

Date override containment ignores slot boundaries

The date override check only rejects slots that end before the override starts or start after the override ends. It does not require slotStartTime >= override start and slotEndTime <= override end. Slots that overlap the beginning or end of a date override are therefore treated as available.

Date override date matching uses inconsistent timezone handling

checkIfIsAvailable computes utcOffset from dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone), then applies it to dayjs(date.start), which is parsed in the server's local timezone, and formats it while slotStartTime is UTC. On a server not set to UTC, the YYYY MM DD comparison can mismatch, causing date overrides to be missed or misapplied.

Timezone adjustment for date overrides drops day shifts

When converting date overrides to minutes, the code adds the timezone offset and then takes only hour() and minute(). If the offset moves the override across midnight, the day shift is discarded. Combined with the activeOverrides filter that does not account for the shifted date, overrides can be generated on the wrong invitee day for large timezone differences.

No regression test for round-robin fixed-host date overrides

The PR description says it fixes date overrides for fixed hosts in round-robin events, but the added test only covers a personal event date override in a different attendee timezone. There is no automated test creating a round-robin event with a fixed host and asserting that slots outside the fixed host's date override are removed.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

Retry-count cleanup is not limited to SMS reminders

The deleteMany query uses an OR branch with a bare `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` condition. That condition is not scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, so this SMS cron job can delete any WorkflowReminder row (including EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders) once its retryCount exceeds 1. The retry-based deletion should be scoped to SMS reminders, and likely to unscheduled SMS reminders, to avoid deleting unrelated reminder rows.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same bug: the deleteMany OR clause's retryCount > 1 condition is not scoped to the SMS method, so non-SMS reminders such as Email and WhatsApp get deleted.

false_positives.candidate:
Reminders with no message or no sendTo never increment retryCount

When `message` is empty or `sendTo` is falsy, the code skips the SMS scheduling call but does not update `retryCount`, mark the reminder as failed, or delete it. Such reminders remain `scheduled: false` and will be selected again on every cron run until their scheduledDate passes. Using `updateMany`, ignoring not-found errors, or wrapping this update in its own try/catch would be safer.

Any exception is treated as an SMS scheduling failure, including failures after Twilio scheduling

In that case the Twilio scheduled message exists, but `scheduled` and `referenceId` may not be persisted, so the reminder remains unscheduled in the database and may be scheduled again on a later run. In handleCancelBooking, when cancelling all remaining recurring events and a calendar reference has a credentialId, the code loops over all of the organizer's calendar credentials and deletes the first calendar reference found on each updated booking. It ignores the specific credentialId/externalCalendarId being processed and repeats this for every calendar reference. With multiple calendar references this causes duplicate or cross-credential delete attempts and can miss non-organizer credentials fetched from the DB.

await apiDeletes does not await the queued deletion promises

In the paid cancellation branch, apiDeletes is an array of promises from calendar/video deletion calls, but the code executes await apiDeletes. Awaiting an array does not wait for the promises inside it, so the handler can return before deletions complete and rejected promises may become unhandled. It should use Promise.all or Promise.allSettled on apiDeletes.

The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getCalendar does not handle dynamic import failures

getCalendar awaits appStore[...] where each entry is now a dynamic import promise. If the app chunk fails to load, that promise rejects. The function signature and most callers expect Calendar or null and handle null, but they do not necessarily handle exceptions. Without a try/catch around the import, a missing or broken app chunk can turn an unsupported calendar into a thrown error and break booking, cancellation, or reschedule flows.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments raise the same concern: the awaited dynamic import has no try/catch, so an import failure is not handled gracefully. The candidate makes this point explicitly and adds detail about the effect on callers.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Async calendar/video cleanup is not awaited in Reschedule

bookingRefsFiltered.forEach is passed an async callback. forEach does not await those callbacks, so the surrounding try/catch cannot catch rejections from getCalendar, deleteEvent, or deleteMeeting. The function proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before remote events are actually deleted. This can leave stale calendar/video events and cause unhandled promise rejections. Use Promise.all with map and await the result.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same problem: forEach with async callbacks for calendar/video deletion is not awaited. This causes unhandled rejections and incomplete cleanup, and the surrounding try/catch is ineffective. Both also suggest the same fix, Promise.all with map.

false_positives.candidate:
Reschedule cleanup promises are fire-and-forget

In requestReschedule, bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) is not awaited. Calendar and video deletions run in the background, errors are not caught, and sendRequestRescheduleEmail/webhooks execute before deletions complete. This can leave stale events and produce unhandled promise rejections. Use Promise.all with map and await the deletions before sending notifications.

Recurring cancellation deletes are not awaited and are lost from apiDeletes

In the recurring cancellation branch, credentials.forEach(async ...) is not awaited. The callback awaits getCalendar and deleteEvent and then pushes resolved values into apiDeletes, so the outer code cannot reliably wait for those deletions; apiDeletes may be incomplete when Promise.all is called. Rejections are unhandled and recurring calendar events may remain undeleted. Use Promise.all over the async work and push deletion promises instead of awaited values.

await apiDeletes does not wait for the promises in the array

apiDeletes is an array of promises, but awaiting the array itself does not wait for its elements or catch rejections. In the paid cancellation path, the handler can return success while calendar/video deletions are still pending or have failed. Use await Promise.all(apiDeletes) to actually wait for and propagate integration deletion errors.

getCalendarCredentials now returns calendar promises without an async API

getCalendar became async, but getCalendarCredentials still calls it without await and returns objects whose calendar property is now a Promise. Only getConnectedCalendars in this file was updated to await item.calendar. Any other consumer of the exported getCalendarCredentials may now receive a Promise where it previously received Calendar or null, causing incorrect truthiness checks or runtime type errors. Make getCalendarCredentials async and await the calendars, or update and document all consumers.

createMeeting can reject before its Cal Video fallback can run

createMeeting awaits getVideoAdapters outside the try/catch that implements the Cal Video fallback. Since getVideoAdapters now awaits dynamic app imports, a rejected import or app lookup will throw from createMeeting instead of triggering the fallback. Move the await into the try block or catch adapter-loading errors so fallback behavior works.

One failing video app import aborts all video adapter operations

getVideoAdapters awaits each appStore import without catching errors. If one credential maps to a broken or missing app module, the whole function rejects, causing getBusyVideoTimes, createMeeting, updateMeeting, or deleteMeeting to fail even for other valid credentials. Catch per-credential import errors and skip the failing adapter instead of aborting the entire operation.

All app dynamic imports are started eagerly

appStore calls import() for every app during module initialization. This starts loading all app chunks immediately rather than lazily loading only the requested app, and it stores promises without catch. If an import rejects before it is awaited, it can also produce an unhandled rejection. Consider lazy getters or a loader function with error handling if code-splitting and graceful failure are intended.
